title: Exact cyclic normalization for an abelian category with autoequivalence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be an additive exact autoequivalence, and let $m\ge1$. Define $\operatorname{Cyc}_m(\mathcal C,P)$ to have objects $(A_i,a_i)_{0\le i<m}$ with isomorphisms $a_i:A_{i+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_i$ for $i<m-1$ and $a_{m-1}:P^mA_0\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{m-1}$. Its morphisms are tuples $u_i:A_i\to A_i'$ satisfying $u_i a_i=a_i'u_{i+1}$ for $i<m-1$ and $u_{m-1}a_{m-1}=a_{m-1}'P^m(u_0)$; identities and composition are componentwise. Write $\mathcal C^{P^m}$ for the fixed-pair category of [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category].

The return assignment
$$T(A_i,a_i)=(A_0,a_0\circ\cdots\circ a_{m-1}),\qquad T(u_i)=u_0$$
is an exact equivalence $\operatorname{Cyc}_m(\mathcal C,P)\simeq\mathcal C^{P^m}$. Its specified quasi-inverse $S$ sends $(A,\phi)$ to $A_i=A$, $a_i=\operatorname{id}_A$ for $i<m-1$, $a_{m-1}=\phi$, and sends $u$ to the constant tuple $u_i=u$. One has $TS=\operatorname{id}$; the natural isomorphism $\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}ST$ has components $r_0=\operatorname{id}_{A_0}$ and $r_i=a_0\circ\cdots\circ a_{i-1}:A_i\xrightarrow{\sim}A_0$ for $i>0$.

Both categories are abelian. In the cyclic category kernels and cokernels are computed componentwise; in the fixed-pair category they are computed on the underlying objects of $\mathcal C$. The induced structure maps are invertible, and a sequence is exact if and only if it is exact on those underlying objects. Consequently $T,S$ identify subobjects, their quotients and arbitrary finite filtrations, in both directions. For $m=1$ the cyclic and fixed-pair descriptions coincide and there are no intermediate arrows.

proof.text: Construct the return functor by composing the closing structure isomorphism with the recursively defined partial products. Each intermediate morphism square gives partial-product naturality by finite induction. The final square gives return naturality; the zeroth component therefore defines the algebra morphism. Define the inverse on the specified constant tuple and constant component maps. Transporting the component evaluation functors along Fin.lastCases equations verifies the structured morphism equations.

The partial-product isomorphisms define a structured unit, and their naturality proves it is natural. On a constant tuple every partial product is the identity, so the return structure is the original structure. Take the identity carrier counit. The zeroth partial product is the identity, proving the triangle identity. Extensionality of fixed pairs and functors gives the strict equality of inverse followed by return. This includes n=0 without a separate construction.

Induct on iteration to prove additivity and equivalence of every power of P. Each twisted-shift component is evaluation or evaluation followed by the power. It is additive and preserves finite limits and colimits. Use the pointwise preservation criteria and the evaluation comparison natural isomorphism to prove the same for the twisted shift. Apply the existing IsoAlgebra.abelian and its exact forgetful functor instances in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.EndoFunctor to the shift and the power. These implement the componentwise kernel, cokernel and coimage-image argument. Evaluation and forgetting preserve finite limits and colimits.

Use ShortComplex.exact_map_iff_of_faithful for the faithful exact fixed-pair forgetful functors, and ShortComplex.exact_iff_evaluation for the discrete diagram category. The return morphism formula proves additivity directly, and the inverse is additive by the additive equivalence instance. Equivalences preserve finite limits and colimits and are faithful; exact_map_iff_of_faithful gives both exactness equivalences.

For any additive equivalence E, lower MonoOver.congr to subobjects and convert that categorical equivalence to an order isomorphism. Its value on a subobject is Subobject.mk(E.map U.arrow), by quotient induction. The representative isomorphisms identify the inclusions for U≤V with E.map(Subobject.ofLE U V); cancel the mapped monic ambient inclusion to verify the square. Compose PreservesCokernel.iso with cokernel.mapIso for the quotient comparison. Compose finite chains pointwise with this order isomorphism and its inverse, and prove inverse identities pointwise. Apply this proved general argument to the normalization and its inverse. Empty chains are included.
